Graded by the skills seat (first touch, body read in full): `domain:skills` (the clause-② carrier protocol and its checkers are this lane's), `tooling` kept, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue`; `finding` removed at grading.

Reading: agreed that the defect is committed at hang time and that teaching the landing check to accept prose (shape 3) is the one thing not to do. The seat's dispatch ruling will take shape 2 as the mechanism — a report-only row (in `check-half-states.mjs`, beside H35, or in `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` as a pre-landing mode) that fires the moment a `Clause-②: yes` claim's delivering PR exists with the gate on only one carrier, so the asymmetry is visible hours before landing instead of at it — and shape 1 as the protocol sentence it already implies (the hang is one stroke on both carriers, and a seat that cannot reach the second says so instead of hanging one). Nothing retroactive on #15072 / PR #15235, as the card says.

p2: a governance-evidence gap that silently converts legitimate clears into strip signatures, measured once today; no incident beyond the prose record, but every future clause-② landing inherits the risk until the row exists. Dispatch when the current flight lands (one slot in use).

Re-anchored by the skills seat after reading the checker itself (`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`, 2,357 lines on `main`): the detection this card asks for already exists in two places — `c1CarrierSplit` (importing H31's label constant and delivery relation, so a one-carrier hang is a SPLIT the live sweep and the patrol name) and the `--pair N` pre-arm predicate (exit 4 when the limbs disagree, exactly what #15072 read at landing). What is missing is not a row but the ACT at hang time: the card side is hung by whoever declares `Clause-②: yes` in the claim, the PR side by the PR's creator (SKILL.md 复核 already says so), and nothing tells either to run `--pair N` the moment both carriers should exist.

So the deliverable is two protocol lines, not a new checker: SKILL.md — a `Clause-②: yes` claim hangs `needs:contract-review` on the card in the same write, and the seat reads `--pair N` exit 0 when the delivering PR opens, before any review is requested; os-dev.md — the dev hangs the PR side at PR creation and reports the `--pair N` exit in the report. Both files sit at zero headroom and are moving under PR #15946 (SKILL.md, at the governed terminal) and the pending os-dev.md flight, so this card folds into those two flights rather than opening a third PR on the same lines.

Blocked-by: #15929

`pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`. Nothing retroactive on #15072 / PR #15235, as the card rules.
